test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 Oct 2021 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Last year 300 students appeared for an examination from school A, and 33(1)/(3)% of the students failed. In the same year, 480 students appeared for the examination from school B,, What is the fail percentage of students from school B if a total of 60% students got passed from both schools?
solution:
**Given:**

Total number of students in school A = 300

Number of students failed in school A = 33(1)/(3)% 

Total number of students in school B = 480

60% of the total students from schools A and B passed

**Calculation:**

Total number of students in school A = 300

Number of students failed in school A = 33(1)/(3)% 

⇒ (300 × 100/300) = 100

Now,

Total number of students in school A and B = (300 + 480) = 780

60% of the total students from schools A and B passed

⇒ (780 × 60/100)

⇒ 468

Number of failed students from school A and B = (780 – 468)

⇒ 312

Fail student from school B = (312 – 100) = 212

Fail% of students from school B = (212/480 × 100)

⇒ (265/6)

⇒ 44(1)/(6)%

**∴ The required percentage of failed students in school B is 44(1)/(6)**
